title: Add concurrency-heatmap prober and gradual-pause rollout gate
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Add a new probe to detect concentrated concurrency hotspots and a rollout gate that gradually pauses canary traffic when hotspots are detected. Improves detection of tail-latency regressions caused by uneven concurrency distribution and reduces noisy rollbacks.
body:
Context: We regularly observe tail-latency regressions that are not correlated with aggregate p95/p99 shifts but instead manifest as short-lived, high-intensity concurrency hotspots (e.g. sudden affinity to a small subset of routes, backend shard hotness, or scheduler alignment effects). These regressions frequently evade existing canary detectors which rely on aggregated distributions and throughput-weighted signals, resulting in either missed regressions or noisy false positives.

This change introduces two complementary pieces:
1) Concurrency Heatmap Prober — a lightweight continuous probe that builds a temporal heatmap of concurrency by traffic key (route/service/shard tag). The probe tracks short-window occupancy and concentration metrics (entropy, top-k mass, burstiness index) and exposes a probabilistic risk score for hotspot-driven tail events.
2) Gradual Pause Rollout Gate — a rollout guard that uses the heatmap risk score to apply a controlled, staged pause to canary traffic (not a hard rollback). Instead of flipping from go -> rollback, the gate reduces canary traffic in configurable micro-steps while continuing targeted probes to validate whether the hotspot dissipates. This reduces churn and gives the scheduler/time-based factors a chance to stabilize.

Design highlights and motivation: The heatmap uses reservoir sampling per traffic key with time-decayed counts; this allows bounded memory with recency bias. We compute entropy and top-3 mass and combine them into a single risk score using a small probabilistic model (logistic blending with configurable thresholds). The Gradual Pause Gate consumes that score and performs staged traffic corking with exponential backoff windows. This approach is intentionally orthogonal to existing percentile-based detectors so the system can reason about regressions caused by concentrated concurrency vs. global latency shifts.

Compatibility and safety: All toggles live behind runtime feature flags and a canary-policy predicate. Default behavior is off. When enabled, the gate defaults to conservative thresholds (first stage: 25% traffic reduction, probe budget 5% of normal requests) and never pauses traffic below a minimum availability floor. The change contains multiple safe-guards: minimum probe sampling, circuit-breaker on probe flakiness, and telemetry rollbacks if probe success rate drops.

What I changed (high-level):
- pkg/canary/probers/heatmap_prober.go — core heatmap logic, reservoir sampling, risk scoring
- pkg/canary/gates/gradual_pause_gate.go — rollout gate implementation and state machine
- pkg/canary/config/defaults.yaml — new config knobs for heatmap bins, smoothing, pause stages
- pkg/telemetry/metrics.go — new metrics (concurrency_heat_entropy, concurrency_top_mass, heatmap_risk_score, gradual_pause_stage)
- internal/e2e/canary_heatmap_test.go — integration tests with synthetic hotspot loads
- dashboards/canary_heatmap.json — Grafana dashboard focused on probe visualization
- docs/operations/canary_heatmap.md — operator guide, tuning advice and runbook

Testing and QA: unit tests for reservoir logic, property tests for decay behavior, and an e2e harness that simulates skewed traffic (100x intensity on 2 of 1k keys) to validate detection and staged pause. Added load profiles to perf-lab and ran a 24-hour soak with randomized scheduler alignments to ensure no stability regressions. We also exercised the circuit-breaker by forcing probe failures to validate safe rollback behavior.

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind feature flag. Stage rollout to staging clusters with gradual rollout (10% accounts) for 48h, then increase to 50% if no incident. If the gate triggers >3 times in 24h for the same service, ops alert routes to SRE for manual triage.

Open questions / TODOs: bind heatmap keys to richer runtime labels (per-customer affinity) — future follow-up (ENG-9739). Consider adding a hierarchical heatmap that aggregates by service -> route -> host for faster triage.

Notes: All description sections above are kept here as a single continuous string for GitHub PR body export.

review_thread:
Evan Liu (2026-01-26): "Looks promising. Can you clarify memory bounds for the reservoir sampler and worst-case CPU for scoring?"
Samira Patel (2026-01-26): "Reservoir uses fixed per-key capacity (default 128 samples) and samples are time-decayed; worst-case scoring is O(keys_in_window) but we cap active keys via an LRU eviction at 10k keys per node. Added comments and a config knob for the cap."
Aisha Rao (2026-01-27): "Please add an explainer in the docs for ops to tune pause-stage sizes. Also, please make the default feature flag off for stable clusters."
Samira Patel (2026-01-27): "Done: added ops tuning section and set default feature flag to off. Also added minimum availability floor so no rollout can reduce service below 50% by default."
Miguel Hernandez (2026-01-29): "Integration test flake: the e2e harness sometimes fails when scheduler alignment happens; can we make the probe timing jittered to avoid deterministic race?"
Samira Patel (2026-01-30): "Adjusted the probe schedule to add randomized jitter and re-ran the suite. CI rerun passed locally. Added the note to the test to avoid future flakes."
Evan Liu (2026-02-01): "Approve after CI green and a quick prow job review. Would like to monitor metric cardinality once deployed."
Aisha Rao (2026-02-02): "LGTM. Recommended follow-up: add alert runbook hook and link to SRE playbook."
ci_summary: Initial CI: unit tests ran and lint found missing godoc in heatmap_prober.go (fixed). Integration e2e failed once due to deterministic scheduling in test (addressed with jitter). Rerun: all checks passed (unit, integration-e2e, linters, security-scan). Coverage delta: +0.6%. Canary-e2e took ~18m; perf-lab smoke profile executed in staged pipeline. No secrets or license issues detected.
